exact_passage: 1.1 The three components of $\widetilde F$ are $(x,y,z)\mapsto P(x,y)$, $(x,y,z)\mapsto Q(x,y)$ and the constant $0$. Their first partial derivatives are $\partial_x\widetilde F_x=\partial_xP$, $\partial_y\widetilde F_x=\partial_yP$, $\partial_z\widetilde F_x=0$; $\partial_x\widetilde F_y=\partial_xQ$, $\partial_y\widetilde F_y=\partial_yQ$, $\partial_z\widetilde F_y=0$; and all three of $\partial_x\widetilde F_z$, $\partial_y\widetilde F_z$, $\partial_z\widetilde F_z$ are $0$. Each of these exists and is continuous on $U\times\mathbb R$ because $P$ and $Q$ are $C^1$ on $U$, so $\widetilde F$ is $C^1$ there by [F2]. [given, F2, F5]
explanation: The planar lift is defined on the open product neighborhood, with z-derivatives zero and both other curl components zero. The finite elementary Green theorem directly supplies the integral identity; the proof does not invoke classical Stokes and therefore does not create the circle discussed in its remark.

exact_passage: 1.1 Fix one nondegenerate rectangle $Q\supseteq A$; since each $A_i\subseteq A$, the same $Q$ bounds every one of the $N+1$ sets. Write $\widetilde f$ for the zero extension of $f$ from $A$ to $Q$ and $\widetilde f_i$ for the zero extension of $f|_{A_i}$ from $A_i$ to $Q$. By hypothesis and [F1], with [L1] licensing the common choice of $Q$, all $N+1$ of these functions are integrable over $Q$, with $\int_Q\widetilde f=\int_Af$ and $\int_Q\widetilde f_i=\int_{A_i}f$. If $m=1$, the boundary of $Q=[u,v]$ is the two-point set $\{u,v\}$, and each point has content zero because for every $\varepsilon>0$ it lies in a closed interval of length below $\varepsilon$; if $m>1$, the boundary of $Q$ is the finite union of its coordinate faces, each a continuous graph over a compact nondegenerate rectangle, so [L5] makes every face content zero. Thus $\partial Q$ has content zero by [F2] in every dimension, and therefore $Q$ is Jordan measurable by [L4]. [given, F1, F2, L1, L4, L5]
explanation: All zero extensions are integrable over one common bounding rectangle by the given individual integrability and its rectangle-independence supplier. Their finite linear combination vanishes outside finitely many content-zero overlaps and the residue. The epsilon divided by N(N-1)+1 cover argument proves this union content zero; invariance then gives the integral identity. The product argument mentioned in the remark is not needed because piece integrability is an explicit hypothesis.
